what: Bun compile (and Node SEA) provide MINIMAL source protection in 2026. Public tools lafkpages/bun-decompile and vibheksoni/unbuned extract readable JS from Bun binaries in seconds. Someone already reverse-engineered Anthropic's Claude Code Bun binary and published it. Node SEA is even weaker — blob is documented by Node.js itself, extractable via objcopy/strings. For the aide-memory binary migration goal of "source hidden" both of these are too weak. Meaningfully better pure-JS option: yao-pkg (active fork of deprecated vercel/pkg, v6.18 Apr 2026) compiles JS to V8 bytecode by default. Bytecode requires Ghidra + specialized decompiler plugin to reverse — raises cost from seconds to hours. yao-pkg also handles better-sqlite3 natively (no Bun-compile ABI / /$bunfs/ problem). For stronger protection: layer javascript-obfuscator before packaging, or commercial Jscrambler/JSDefender for polymorphic obfuscation + RASP. For REAL protection against determined reversal: move sensitive logic to Rust N-API addon — no TS→native transpiler exists in 2026. upstream better-sqlite3 will NOT support Bun (issue #16050 closed as wontfix, dup of #4290).
why: Fundamentally revises the binary migration's protection calculus. Memory 136 listed alternatives but treated Bun as reasonable protection — agent research shows Bun is basically "obfuscation, not hiding". yao-pkg bytecode mode is strictly better AND skips the better-sqlite3 Bun-compile blocker entirely. Any future phase spawn weighing Bun vs alternatives should have this corrected framing.
